• Swayambhu is an ancient religious complex atop a hill in the Kathmandu Valley, west of Kathmandu city. 
 
• The stupa has stood as a hallmark of faith and harmony for centuries with Hindu temples and deities incorporated in this Buddhist site.
 
• This stupa is the oldest of its kind in Nepal and has numerous shrines and monasteries on its premises.

• The Swayambunath complex suffered damage in the April 2015 Nepal earthquake.

questions.question: In which of the following place, are the Dilwara temples of Jainism located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mount Abu**__.

**Dilwara temples of Jainism located at Mount Abu.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dilwara Jain Temples** is one of the finest Jain temples known in world for its **extraordinary architecture and marvelous marble stone carvings **and are located at **Mount Abu.**
 
• These temples were built between the **11th to 13th Centuries AD.**
 
• All this was done at a time when no transport or roads were available at a height of 1200+ Mtrs in Mount Abu. 
 
• Huge blocks of marble stones were transported on elephant backs from the Arasoori Hills at Ambaji to this remote hilly region of Mount Abu. 
 
• Dilwara temples are also a popular **Jain pilgrimage attraction**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Dilwara Temple complex consists of** five major sections or temples devoted to five Jain Tirthankaras (Saints)**:

 
 
• Shri Mahaveer Swami Temple 
 
• Shri AdiNath Temple or Vimal Vasahi Temple
 
• Shri ParshavNath Temple or Khartar Vasahi Temple
 
• Shri Rishabdaoji Temple or Peethalhar Temple 
 
• Shri NemiNathJi Temple or Luna Vasahi Temple

questions.question: With which of the following is the term 'Vesara' associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Temple Architecture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**It is a hybridized style of Nagara and Dravida style of temple architecture.

__
 
• It became popular after the mid-seventh century in the region of Karnataka, under the patronage of Chalukyas rulers.
 
• Features of Vesara **style:
 
 
• Compound walls may or may not be present.
 
• Gopurams may or may not be present.
 
• The plan of these temples looks like a star and is thus known as a stellate plan.
 
• Examples: Durga Temple (Aihole), Virupaksh Temple (Pattadkal), Keshava Temple (Somnathpur) , Halebidu.
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The temple architecture in India is not the same everywhere.
 
• Basically there are three styles of temple architecture in India:

 
• Nagara Style (North India)
 
• Dravida Style (South India)
 
• Vasara style (Mix of Nagara and Dravida style)

 
• Nagara Style:

 
• Built on a stone platform with steps leading up to it.
 
• Have a tower or Shikhara.
 
• Have Grabhagriha ( A place for the idols of god and goddess).
 
• Examples: Kandariya Mahadeo temple at Khajuraho, Lakshamana temple

 
• Dravida Style:

 
• Generally enclosed within a compounded wall.
 
• The entrance gateway is known as Gopuram.
 
• The shape of Temple tower known as Vimana (similar to Shikhara in Nagara style).
 
• Large water tanks are common in the temple complex.
 
• Examples: Brahadeeshwara temple, Rajarajeswara temple.

 
• Vasara style:

 
• This style of temple architecture is a mix of Nagara and Dravid style.
 
• Examples: Dodda Basappa Temple, Hoysala Temple

• It is based on **Dravidian **Architecture and a **UNESCO** World Heritage Site.
 
• This temple is dedicated to **Lord Shiva.​**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

• Virupaksha Temple: located on the banks of Tungabhadra river in Hampi in Karnataka and dedicated to Lord Virupaksha, a form of Lord Shiva. It was built by Lakkan Dandesha of Vijayanagar empire.
 
• Badami Cave Temple: Hindu and Jain cave temples in Badami in Karnataka representing Indian rock-cut architecture. There are 4 caves dedicated to Lord Shiva (Nataraja form), Lord Vishnu (Trivikrama form) and Jain figures.

questions.question: Temple architecture in South India attained its climax under the rule of the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cholas.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• Temple architecture in South India attained its climax under the rule of the **Cholas.**

 
• The Chola empire was founded by Vijayalaya in the 9th century.
 
• The capital of Chola was Tanjore.
 
• The style of architecture during this period is called Dravida, which is now known as th**e "Great Living Chola Temples".**
 
• Chola temples often became the nuclei of settlements that grew around them.
 
• These were centres of craft production.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some of the temples built by Cholas are as follows. 
 
• Brihadisvara Temple at Thanjavur.
 
 
• It was built during the reign of the Chola emperor Rajaraja and designed by the famous architect Sama Varma between 1003 and 1010 AD.
 
• It is enthroned with a 13-story pyramidal pinnacle, the Vimana, standing 66 m high and finished off with a bulb-formed stone monument. 
 
 
 
• The Brihadisvara Temple at Gangaikondacholisvaram. 
 
 
• ​It was made by the Chola head Rajendra I. 
 
• It is portrayed as the female partner of the Thanjavur temple. 
 
 
 
• Airavatesvara Temple at Darasuram.
 
 
• It was constructed by Rajaraja II and the temple is devoted to Lord Shiva. 
 
• This temple has six sets of gigantic, solid dvarapalas sculptures guarding the passages and bronzes of exceptional magnificence inside.

questions.question: What does the Panchayatana style refer to?

options.text: A dance form of South India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __A temple architecture.__

__
 
• Panchayatana is a style of **temple construction** that has a **central shrine** surrounded by** four other shrines.**
 
• **Examples of Panchayatana temples.**
 
• **Jagdish Temple** in Udaipur.
 
• **Lakshmana Temple** in Khajuraho.
 
• **Kandariya Mahadeva Temple** in Khajuraho.
 
• **Brahmeswara Temple** in Bhubaneswar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aad650d98ae0197c18fbe0754b593721cb8c1898493f61790d81f72b924f2fc5.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Nagara Style of Temple Architecture**
 **Dravidian Style of Temple Architecture**
 
 

 Temples located in **Northern India** are classified as **Nagara **Style.
 Temples located in **Southern India** are classified as **Dravidian Style.**
 
 

 Nagara Style has **multiple Shikharas.**
 The Dravidian style has **1 single Shikhara**.
 
 

 In Nagara Style, Central Tower is **Curvilinear** in shape.
 In Dravidian Style, Central Tower is shaped like a **Pyramid.**
 
 

 In Nagara style, pedestals are higher than the **ground.**
 Pedestals are at **ground level** in the Dravidian Style.
 
 

 In the Nagara style, the** most **prominent element is the **Shikhara**.
 In Dravidian Style, the most prominent element is the **Gopuram**.

questions.question: Which among the following is located in Mount Abu?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Dilwara Temple**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Dilwara Temples** are a group of Jain svetambara temples situated about 2.5 kilometres from the settlement of Mount Abu, the only hill station in Rajasthan.
 
• The earliest were built by Vimal Shah and allegedly planned or at least funded by Vastupala, Dholka's Jain minister.
 
• They date from the 11th and 16th centuries, creating some of the most prominent monuments in the architectural style of Māru-Gurjara, renowned for their use of very pure white marble and intricate carvings of marble. Among the most renowned Jain temples are the five Dilwara Temples.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• The five temples are:
 
 
• **Vimal Vasahi: **This temple dedicated to the first Jain Tirthankara, Shri Adinatha
 
• **Luna Vasahi: **This temple dedicated to the 22nd Jain Tirthankara, Shri Neminatha
 
• **Pittalhar:** This temple dedicated to the first Jain Tirthankar, Shri Adinatha
 
• **Parshvanath: **This temple dedicated to the 23rd Jain Tirthankara, Shri Parshvanatha
 
• **Mahavir Swami: **This temple dedicated to the last Jain Tirthankara, Shri Mahaviraswami
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Saheliyon-ki-Bari** is a large garden and a popular tourist spot in Udaipur, Rajasthan.
 
• At the edge of the Aravalli Hills stands **Nahargarh Fort,** overlooking the city of Jaipur in Rajasthan.
 
• In the town of Bansberia in Hooghly District, West Bengal,** Hanseswari temple** is a Hindu temple of the goddess Hangseswari (the goddess who came in the dream of Raja Nrisingha Deb Roy Mahasay).

questions.question: The southern most Jyotirlinga temple is located in which Indian state?

questions.question: Pandharpur was a medieval centre for the worship of:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Vithoba**__.

__
 
• **Pandharpur **was a **medieval center** for the **worship of Vithoba**.
 
• Pandharpur is situated in** Maharashtra**.
 
• **Shri Vitthal Rukmini temple** is also known as the **Vithoba temple.**
 
• **God Vithoba** is worshipped in this temple.
 
• **A form of Vishnu** or Krishna is **God Vithoba**.
 
• A procession is started by the Warkaris from their home to this temple to reach Aashadi and Kartiki Ekadashi.
 
• This procession is also known a**s Dindi.**

 

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Pandharpur is situated on the bank of the **River Chandrabhaga**.
 
• It is believed that by dipping in this River, all sin will be washed out.
 
• The women and people from backward caste were invited to this temple for the first time in 2014.
